arXiv:nlin/0609058v1 [nlin.SI] 24 Sep 2006

Direct integral method, complete discrimination system for polynomial and applications to classifications of all single traveling wave solutions to nonlinear differential equations:a survey

Chengshi Liu Affiliation: Department of Mathematics Affiliation: Daqing Petroleum Institute Affiliation: Daqing 163318, China Affiliation: Email: chengshiliu-68@126.com Email: csliu@dqpi.edu.cn
Abstract

Complete discrimination system for polynomial and direct integral method were discussed systematically. In particularly, we pointed out some mistaken viewpoints. Combining with complete discrimination system for polynomial, direct integral method was developed to become a powerful method and was applied to a lot of nonlinear mathematical physics equations. All single traveling wave solutions to theses equations can be obtained. As examples, we gave all traveling wave solutions to some equations such as mKdV equation, Sine-Gordon equation ,Double Sine-Gordon equation, triple Sine-Gordon equation, Fujimoto-Watanabe equation, coupled Harry-Dym equation and coupled KdV equation and so on. At the end, we give the partial answers to Fan’s a problem.

Keywords: complete discrimination system for polynomial, direct integral method, traveling wave solution, nonlinear differential equation

PACS: 02.30.Jr, 05.45.Yv

1 Introduction

In order to solve the traveling wave solutions to some nonlinear evolution equations, sometimes these equations are reduced to an ordinary differential equations such as

u′​(ξ)=G⁡(u,θ1,⋯,θm),u^{\prime}(\xi)=G(u,\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{m}), (1)

where θ1,⋯,θm\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{m} are parameters,its solutions can be wrote by integral form

ξ−ξ0=∫d​uG⁡(u,θ1,⋯,θm).\xi-\xi_{0}=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{G(u,\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{m})}. (2)

Thus what we need is only to solve the integral (2). According to different parameters, we will give different solution to the integral. This is so called direct integral method. Although direct integral method is a routine method, but to decide the parameter’s scope is still rather difficult. Thus the most important steps are to decide the parameter’s scopes and the corresponding integral solutions. A new mathematical tool named complete discrimination system for polynomial([1-5]) is applied to this problem so that the parameter’s scopes is solved.

It is just because of combining with complete discrimination system that direct integral method becomes a powerful and efficient method. There are a lot of nonlinear mathematical physics equations such as KdV equation, Hirota equation, breaking soliton equation, Coupled mKdV equation,Chen-lee-Liu equation, Kundu equation equation,cubic Schrödinger equation, Sine-Gordon equation, double Sine-Gordon equation, Sinh-Gordon equation, double Sinh-Gordon equation, triple Sinh-Gordon equation, Combine KdV-mKdV equation and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation and so on, their all traveling wave solutions can be obtained by using direct integral method. These complete results can’t be obtained by other any indirect methods ( see [6-19]) such as trial equation method([19]), Jacobi elliptic function expanse method ([12]), sub-equation method([15,16] and homogenous balance method and so on.

Although direct integral method is the most basic method, but there are two obvious mathematical facts about the integral(2) to be ignored. One fact is that different variable transformation don’t offer to a different solution, different variable transformation only give different representation of solution. Another fact is that it is just different parameter’s scope to offer to different solution. Some authors didn’t notice the fact one([20-23]), they still think that a new variable transformation can bring new solutions. We must point out that this is a mistaken viewpoint. In fact, the elementary calculus tell us that a defined function has infinite primitive functions which are different each other by a constant, and that a new variable transformation only offer to a new representation of the primitive function.

In the present paper, using complete discrimination system for polynomial and direct integral method ,we give the classifications of all single traveling wave solutions to a lot of nonlinear differential equations such as mKdV equation and Sine-Gordon equation, Fujimoto-Watanabe equation, coupled Harry-Dym equation and coupled KdV equation and so on. An the end, we give the partial answer to Fan’s a problem.

This paper is organized as follows. In section 2, we deal with some equations whose reduced ODE’s take the form of (u′)2=a3​u3+a2​u2+a1​u+a0(u^{\prime})^{2}=a_{3}u^{3}+a_{2}u^{2}+a_{1}u+a_{0}, and obtain the classifications of all single traveling wave solutions to those equations. In section 3, we deal with some equations whose reduced ODE’s take the form of (u′)2=a4​u4+a3​u3+a2​u2+a1​u+a0(u^{\prime})^{2}=a_{4}u^{4}+a_{3}u^{3}+a_{2}u^{2}+a_{1}u+a_{0}, and obtain the classifications of all single traveling wave solutions to those equations. In section 4, we give some applications of the complete discrimination system for the fifth order polynomial. In section 5, we deal with two equations with rational form of reduced equations and obtain classifications of their all single traveling wave solutions. In section 6, we use a one-parameter’s thick obtain the classifications of all single traveling wave solutions to some equations such as coupled KdV equation and so on. In section 7, we discuss Fan’s two problems, and give an answer to the first problem.

2 Applications of the complete discrimination system for the third order polynomial

There are a lot of nonlinear evolution equations such as KdV equation

We take only three equations as examples to illustrate this method, other equations can be dealt with similarly.

Example 1.Classification of all single traveling wave solutions to KdV equation

Although KdV equation is a classical equation, its single traveling wave solutions had been discussed many years ago. But its classification hasn’t been reported, some author also try to give its new single traveling wave solutions, so we take it as an example and give its all single traveling wave solutions. In fact under the traveling wave transformation, KdV equation can be reduced to the following ODE:

(u′)2=−2k2​u3−ωk3​u2+c1​u+c0.(u^{\prime})^{2}=-\frac{2}{k^{2}}u^{3}-\frac{\omega}{k^{3}}u^{2}+c_{1}u+c_{0}. (28)

Thus it is easy to give the classification of all solutions to ODE 28 according to the former results. For briefly we omit them.

Example 2.Classification of all single traveling wave solutions to Sine-Gordon equation.

Sine-Gordon equation reads

ux​t=a​sin⁡u,u_{xt}=a\sin u, (29)

which widely applied in physics and engineering. Its so-called new traveling wave solutions have been obtained in different functional forms by different methods([25-30]). Among these some method([30]) is very complex but not essence and natural. But we must point out that it is very easy to give all traveling wave solutions to Sine-Gordon equation. In the following, we only need elementary integral method to do this thing. Instituting traveling wave transformation u=u⁡(ξ),ξ=k​x+ω​tu=u(\xi),\xi=kx+\omega t into Eq.(29) and integrating once yield

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​u−ak​ω​(cos⁡u−c),\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\sqrt{-\frac{a}{k\omega}(\cos u-c)}}, (30)

where cc is an arbitrary constant. Take variable transformation

u=arccos⁡w,u=\arccos w, (31)

then Eq.(30) becomes

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​wak​ω​(w−1)​(w+1)​(w−c).\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\sqrt{\frac{a}{k\omega}(w-1)(w+1)(w-c)}}. (32)

Firstly we assume ak​ω>0.\frac{a}{k\omega}>0. There are the following three cases to be discussed:

Case 1: c=1,c=1, then we have

u=a​r​c​s​i​n​{2​tanh2⁡(12​2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0))−1};u=arcsin\{2\tanh^{2}(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0}))-1\}; (33)
u=arcsin⁡{2​coth2⁡(12​2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0))−1}.u=\arcsin\{2\coth^{2}(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0}))-1\}. (34)

Case 2: c=−1,c=-1, then we have

u=arcsin⁡{−2​sec2⁡(12​2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0))+1}.u=\arcsin\{-2\sec^{2}(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0}))+1\}. (35)

Case 3: c≠±1,c\neq\pm 1, we reorder 1,−1,c1,-1,c and denote them by α<β<γ\alpha<\beta<\gamma. In fact there are three case such as 1>c>−1,c>1,1>c>-1,c>1, and −1>c-1>c. When α<w<β\alpha<w<\beta, we have

u=arcsin{α+(β−α)sn2(γ−α22​ak​ω(ξ−ξ0)),m)}.u=\arcsin\{\alpha+(\beta-\alpha)\SN^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{\gamma-\alpha}}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0})),m)\}. (36)

When w>γw>\gamma, we have

u=arcsin⁡{OPENγ−β​sn2⁡(γ−α2​2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0)),m)OPENcn2⁡(γ−α2​2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0)),m)},u=\arcsin\{\frac{\gamma-\beta\SN^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{\gamma-\alpha}}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0})),m)}{\CN^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{\gamma-\alpha}}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0})),m)}\}, (37)

where m2=β−αγ−αm^{2}=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{\gamma-\alpha}.

If ak​ω<0,\frac{a}{k\omega}<0, we take w=−v,w=-v, then Eq.(32) becomes

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​v−ak​ω​(v−1)​(v+1)​(v+c).\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\sqrt{-\frac{a}{k\omega}(v-1)(v+1)(v+c)}}. (38)

We have similar three cases:

Case 1: c=1,c=1, then we have

u=−arcsin⁡{2​tanh2⁡(12​−2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0))−1};u=-\arcsin\{2\tanh^{2}(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{-\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0}))-1\}; (39)
u=−arcsin⁡{2​coth2⁡(12​−2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0))−1}.u=-\arcsin\{2\coth^{2}(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{-\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0}))-1\}. (40)

Case 2: c=−1,c=-1, then we have

u=−arcsin⁡{−2​sec2⁡(12​−2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0))+1}.u=-\arcsin\{-2\sec^{2}(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{-\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0}))+1\}. (41)

Case 3: c≠±1,c\neq\pm 1, we reorder 1,−1,c1,-1,c and denote them by α<β<γ\alpha<\beta<\gamma. When α<w<β\alpha<w<\beta, we have

u=−arcsin{α+(β−α)sn2(γ−α2−2​ak​ω(ξ−ξ0)),m)}.u=-\arcsin\{\alpha+(\beta-\alpha)\SN^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{\gamma-\alpha}}{2}\sqrt{-\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0})),m)\}. (42)

When w>γw>\gamma, we have

u=−arcsin⁡{OPENγ−β​sn2⁡(γ−α2​−2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0)),m)OPENcn2⁡(γ−α2​−2​ak​ω​(ξ−ξ0)),m)},u=-\arcsin\{\frac{\gamma-\beta\SN^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{\gamma-\alpha}}{2}\sqrt{-\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0})),m)}{\CN^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{\gamma-\alpha}}{2}\sqrt{-\frac{2a}{k\omega}}(\xi-{\xi}_{0})),m)}\}, (43)

where m2=β−αγ−αm^{2}=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{\gamma-\alpha}.

Example 3. Classification of all single envelope traveling wave solutions to Hirota equation

Hirota equation reads

i​ut+ux​x+2​|u|2​u+i​α​ux​x​x+6​i​α​|u|2​ux=0,\mathrm{i}u_{t}+u_{xx}+2|u|^{2}u+\mathrm{i}\alpha u_{xxx}+6\mathrm{i}\alpha|u|^{2}u_{x}=0, (44)

when α=0\alpha=0, it becomes Schrodinger equation. Take envelope travelling wave transformation u=u⁡(ξ)​exp⁡(η),ξ=x+ω​t,η=p​x+q​tu=u(\xi)\exp(\eta),\xi=x+\omega t,\eta=px+qt, then separating the real part and the imagine part of Eq.(44) yields

(ω+2​p−3​α​p2)​u′+6​α​u2​u′+α​u′′′=0,(\omega+2p-3\alpha p^{2})u^{\prime}+6\alpha u^{2}u^{\prime}+\alpha u^{\prime\prime\prime}=0, (45)
(α​p3−q−p2)​u+2​(1−3​α​p)​u2+(1−3​α​p)​u′′=0.(\alpha p^{3}-q-p^{2})u+2(1-3\alpha p)u^{2}+(1-3\alpha p)u^{\prime\prime}=0. (46)

In order to make the Eq.(45) and the Eq.(46) consistence, the parameters must satisfy the following condition:

ω+2​p−3​α​p2α​p3−q−p2=α1−3​α​p.\frac{\omega+2p-3\alpha p^{2}}{\alpha p^{3}-q-p^{2}}=\frac{\alpha}{1-3\alpha p}. (47)

Under the condition (47), the above two equations become one equation

(u′)2=−u4+α​p3−q−p23​α​p−1​u2+c(u^{\prime})^{2}=-u^{4}+\frac{\alpha p^{3}-q-p^{2}}{3\alpha p-1}u^{2}+c (48)

where cc is an arbitrary constant. The corresponding integral form is

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​u−u4+α​p3−q−p23​α​p−1​u2+c,\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\sqrt{-u^{4}+\frac{\alpha p^{3}-q-p^{2}}{3\alpha p-1}u^{2}+c}}, (49)

in order to solve the above integral, we take the change of variable w=u2w=u^{2}, then the integral becomes

±2​(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​ww⁡(−w2+α​p3−q−p23​α​p−1​w+c),\pm 2(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\sqrt{w(-w^{2}+\frac{\alpha p^{3}-q-p^{2}}{3\alpha p-1}w+c)}}, (50)

Therefore according to the classification of all solutions of the Eq.(15), it is easy to give classification of all single envelope traveling wave solutions of the Hirota equation. We omit concrete expressions for briefly.

3 Applications of the complete discrimination system for the fourth order polynomial

We first write the complete discrimination system for the fourth order polynomial f⁡(w)=w4+p​w2+q​w+rf(w)=w^{4}+pw^{2}+qw+r as follows([4]):

D1=4,D2=−p,D3=8rp−2p3−9q2,D4=4​p4​r−p3​q2+36​p​r​q2−32​r2​p2−274​q4+64​r3,\begin{split}D_{1}=4,D_{2}=-p,D_{3}=8rp-2p^{3}-9q^{2},\\ D_{4}=4p^{4}r-p^{3}q^{2}+36prq^{2}-32r^{2}p^{2}-\frac{27}{4}q^{4}+64r^{3},\end{split}
F2=9​p2−32​p​r.F_{2}=9p^{2}-32pr. (51)

Then we consider the following ODE

(w′​(ξ))2=ϵ⁡(w4+p​w2+q​w+r),(w^{\prime}(\xi))^{2}=\epsilon(w^{4}+pw^{2}+qw+r), (52)

where ϵ=±1.\epsilon=\pm 1. Rewrite Eq.(52) by integral form as follows:

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​wϵ⁡(w4+p​w2+q​w+r).\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\sqrt{\epsilon(w^{4}+pw^{2}+qw+r)}}. (53)

Although Eq.(52) has been studied extensively, some solutions were obtained under some special parameter’s conditions. But we will give in the following the classification of its all solutions. According to the complete discrimination system for polynomial F⁡(w)=w4+p​w2+q​w+rF(w)=w^{4}+pw^{2}+qw+r, there are nine cases to be discussed([4]), we list those results for convenience in the following.

Case 1: D4=0,D3=0,D2<0D_{4}=0,D_{3}=0,D_{2}<0. Then we have

F⁡(w)=((w−l1)2+s12)2,F(w)=((w-l_{1})^{2}+s_{1}^{2})^{2}, (54)

where l1,s1l_{1},s_{1} are real numbers, s1>0s_{1}>0. When ϵ=1\epsilon=1, we have

w=s1​tan⁡[s1​(ξ−ξ0)]+l1.\displaystyle w=s_{1}\tan[s_{1}(\xi-\xi_{0})]+l_{1}. (55)

Case 2: D4=0,D3=0,D2=0D_{4}=0,D_{3}=0,D_{2}=0. Then we have

F⁡(w)=w4.F(w)=w^{4}. (56)

When ϵ=1\epsilon=1, we have

w=−1ξ−ξ0.\displaystyle w=-\frac{1}{\xi-\xi_{0}}. (57)

Case 3: D4=0,D3=0,D2>0,E2=0D_{4}=0,D_{3}=0,D_{2}>0,E_{2}=0. Then we have

F⁡(w)=(w−α)2​(w−β)2,F(w)=(w-\alpha)^{2}(w-\beta)^{2}, (58)

where α,β\alpha,\beta are real numbers, α>β\alpha>\beta. If ϵ=1\epsilon=1, when w>αw>\alpha or w<β,w<\beta, we have

w=β−α2​[coth⁡α−β2​(ξ−ξ0)−1]+β.\displaystyle w=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{2}[\coth\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}(\xi-\xi_{0})-1]+\beta. (59)

When α>w>β,\alpha>w>\beta, we have

w=β−α2​[tanh⁡α−β2​(ξ−ξ0)−1]+β.\displaystyle w=\frac{\beta-\alpha}{2}[\tanh\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}(\xi-\xi_{0})-1]+\beta. (60)

Case 4: D4=0,D3>0,D2>0D_{4}=0,D_{3}>0,D_{2}>0. Then we have

F⁡(w)=(w−α)2​(w−β)​(w−γ),F(w)=(w-\alpha)^{2}(w-\beta)(w-\gamma), (61)

Example 1. Classification of all single travelling wave solutions to mKdV equation.

mKdV equation reads

ut+a​u2​ux+b​ux​x​x=0.u_{t}+au^{2}u_{x}+bu_{xxx}=0. (89)

Its exact traveling wave solutions have been studied extensively([20-23]). But its all traveling wave solutions haven’t been reported. Using direct integral method and complete discrimination system for the fourth order polynomial, we give in the following all traveling wave solutions to mKdV equation.

Take traveling wave transformation as follows:

u=u⁡(ξ),ξ=k​x+ω​t.u=u(\xi),\xi=kx+\omega t. (90)

Instituting Eq.(90) into Eq.(89) and integrating twice yield

(u′)2=A⁡(u4+p​u2+q​u+r),(u^{\prime})^{2}=A(u^{4}+pu^{2}+qu+r), (91)

where

A=−a6​b​k2,p=a​k6​ω,A=-\frac{a}{6bk^{2}},\ \ p=\frac{ak}{6\omega}, (92)

and q,rq,r are two arbitrary constants. Write Eq.(91) by integral form

±ϵ​A​(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​uϵ⁡(u4+p​u2+q​u+r),\pm\sqrt{\epsilon A}(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\sqrt{\epsilon(u^{4}+pu^{2}+qu+r)}}, (93)

where ϵ=±1.\epsilon=\pm 1. If A>0,A>0, we take ϵ=1.\epsilon=1. If A<0,A<0, we take ϵ=−1.\epsilon=-1. According to the former results, we can give the classification of all single traveling wave solutions to MKdV equation, we omit them for briefly.

Example 2. Classification of all single traveling solutions to combined KdV-MKdV equation([40],[16, \cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{CKM2}{}{}]}]) which reads

ut+a​u​ux+b​u2​ux+ux​x​x=0,u_{t}+auu_{x}+bu^{2}u_{x}+u_{xxx}=0, (94)

where aa and bb are physical parameters. Taking traveling wave transformation u=u⁡(ξ1),ξ1=k​x−ω​t,u=u(\xi_{1}),\xi_{1}=kx-\omega t, and instituting it into Eq.(94) and integrating once yields:

(u′)2=a4​u4+a3​u3+a2​u2+a1​u+a0,(u^{\prime})^{2}=a_{4}u^{4}+a_{3}u^{3}+a_{2}u^{2}+a_{1}u+a_{0}, (95)

where

a4=−a6​k2,a3=−b3​k2,a2=ωk3,a_{4}=-\frac{a}{6k^{2}},\ \ a_{3}=-\frac{b}{3k^{2}},\ \ a_{2}=\frac{\omega}{k^{3}}, (96)

and a1,a0a_{1},a_{0} are arbitrary constants. If a<0,a<0, we take transformations as follows:

w=a414​(u+a34​a4),ξ=a414​ξ1.w=a_{4}^{\frac{1}{4}}(u+\frac{a_{3}}{4a_{4}}),\ \ \xi=a_{4}^{\frac{1}{4}}\xi_{1}. (97)

Then Eq.(95) becomes

(w′)2=w4+p​w2+q​u+r,(w^{\prime})^{2}=w^{4}+pw^{2}+qu+r, (98)

where

p=a2a4,q=a4−14​(a338​a42−a2​a32​a4+a1),r=a0−a1​a34​a4+a2​a3216​a42−3​a34256​a43.p=\frac{a_{2}}{\sqrt{a_{4}}},\ \ q=a_{4}^{-\frac{1}{4}}(\frac{a_{3}^{3}}{8a_{4}^{2}}-\frac{a_{2}a_{3}}{2a_{4}}+a_{1}),\ \ r=a_{0}-\frac{a_{1}a_{3}}{4a_{4}}+\frac{a_{2}a_{3}^{2}}{16a_{4}^{2}}-\frac{3a_{3}^{4}}{256a_{4}^{3}}. (99)

If a>0,a>0, we take transformations as follows:

w=(−a4)14​(u+a34​a4),ξ=(−a4)14​ξ1w=(-a_{4})^{\frac{1}{4}}(u+\frac{a_{3}}{4a_{4}}),\ \ \xi=(-a_{4})^{\frac{1}{4}}\xi_{1} (100)

Then Eq.(95) becomes

(w′)2=−(w4+p​w2+q​u+r),(w^{\prime})^{2}=-(w^{4}+pw^{2}+qu+r), (101)

where

p=−a2−a4,q=(−a4)−14​(−a338​a42+a2​a32​a4−a1),r=−a0−a1​a34​a4−a2​a3216​a42+3​a34256​a43.p=-\frac{a_{2}}{\sqrt{-a_{4}}},\ \ q=(-a_{4})^{-\frac{1}{4}}(-\frac{a_{3}^{3}}{8a_{4}^{2}}+\frac{a_{2}a_{3}}{2a_{4}}-a_{1}),\ \ r=-a_{0}-\frac{a_{1}a_{3}}{4a_{4}}-\frac{a_{2}a_{3}^{2}}{16a_{4}^{2}}+\frac{3a_{3}^{4}}{256a_{4}^{3}}. (102)

According to the classification of solutions to ODE (w′)2=±(w4+p​w2+q​w+r)(w^{\prime})^{2}=\pm(w^{4}+pw^{2}+qw+r), we can give all traveling wave solutions to combined KdV-MKdV equation. We omit them for simplicity

Example 3. Classification of all single traveling wave solutions to Konopelchenko-Dubrovsky equation ([31, 32]) which reads

ut=ux​x​x−6​β​u​ux+32​α2​u2​ux−3​wy+3​α​u​ux=0,\displaystyle u_{t}=u_{xxx}-6\beta uu_{x}+\frac{3}{2}\alpha^{2}u^{2}u_{x}-3w_{y}+3\alpha uu_{x}=0, (103)
wx=uy.\displaystyle w_{x}=u_{y}. (104)

Takeing travelling wave transformation u=u⁡(ξ),ξ=k1​x+k2​y+ω​t,u=u(\xi),\xi=k_{1}x+k_{2}y+\omega t, instituting it into Eq.(103) and integrating twice yield the same form equation with Eq.(109):

(u′)2=a4​u4+a3​u3+a2​u2+a1​u+a0,(u^{\prime})^{2}=a_{4}u^{4}+a_{3}u^{3}+a_{2}u^{2}+a_{1}u+a_{0}, (105)

where

a4=α24​k12,a3=α−2​β2​k12,a2=2​(k1​ω−3​k22)k14,a_{4}=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{4k_{1}^{2}},\ \ a_{3}=\frac{\alpha-2\beta}{2k_{1}^{2}},\ \ a_{2}=\frac{2(k_{1}\omega-3k_{2}^{2})}{k_{1}^{4}}, (106)

and a1,a0a_{1},a_{0} are arbitrary constants. Notice a4>0a_{4}>0. According to the example 1, it is easy to write all traveling wave solutions to KD equation, we omit them for briefly. All nine cases under the condition a4>0a_{4}>0 in section 4 are possible.

Example 4: Classification of all single traveling solutions to double Sine-Gordon equation ([42, 43]) which reads

ux​x−ut​t=sin⁡a​u+λ​sin⁡a2​u,u_{xx}-u_{tt}=\sin{au}+\lambda\sin{\frac{a}{2}u}, (107)

where aa and λ\lambda are nonzero constants. Its some exact traveling wave solutions have been obtained. We give in the following its all traveling wave solutions.

Take traveling wave transformation

u=u⁡(ξ1),ξ1=k​x−ω​t,k≠±ω.u=u(\xi_{1}),\ \ \xi_{1}=kx-{\omega}t,\ \ k\neq\pm\omega. (108)

Instituting Eq.(108) into Eq.(107) and integrating once yields

±(ξ1−ξ10)=∫d​uc2−c1​cos⁡a​u−c0​cos⁡a2​u.\pm(\xi_{1}-\xi_{10})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\sqrt{c_{2}-c_{1}\cos{au}-c_{0}\cos{\frac{a}{2}u}}}. (109)

where

c1=2a⁡(k2−ω2),c0=4​λa⁡(k2−ω2).c_{1}=\frac{2}{a(k_{2}-\omega^{2})},c_{0}=\frac{4\lambda}{a(k_{2}-\omega^{2})}. (110)

In order to solve above integral (109), we take transformation as follows:

u=2a​arccos⁡v.u=\frac{2}{a}\arccos{v}. (111)

If c1>0,c_{1}>0, let

w=c1​v+c04​c1,ξ=a2​c1​ξ1.w=\sqrt{c_{1}}v+\frac{c_{0}}{4c_{1}},\ \ \xi=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2c_{1}}}\xi_{1}. (113)

Thus Eq.(112) becomes respectively

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​v(w−α)​(w−β)​(w2+d0).\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\sqrt{(w-\alpha)(w-\beta)(w^{2}+d_{0})}}. (114)

where

α=c04​c1+c1,β=c04​c1−c1,d0=c1−c22−c0214​c12.\displaystyle\alpha=\frac{c_{0}}{4c_{1}}+\sqrt{c_{1}},\ \ \beta=\frac{c_{0}}{4c_{1}}-\sqrt{c_{1}},\ \ d_{0}=\frac{c_{1}-c_{2}}{2}-\frac{c_{0}^{2}}{14c_{1}^{2}}. (115)

If c1<0,c_{1}<0, let

w=−c1​v−c04​c1,ξ=a2​c1​ξ1.w=\sqrt{-c_{1}}v-\frac{c_{0}}{4c_{1}},\ \ \xi=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2c_{1}}}\xi_{1}. (116)

Thus Eq.(112) becomes respectively

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​v−(w−α)​(w−β)​(w2+d0).\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\sqrt{-(w-\alpha)(w-\beta)(w^{2}+d_{0})}}. (117)

where

α=−c04​c1+−c1,β=−c04​c1−−c1,d0=c1−c22−c0214​c12.\displaystyle\alpha=-\frac{c_{0}}{4c_{1}}+\sqrt{-c_{1}},\ \ \beta=-\frac{c_{0}}{4c_{1}}-\sqrt{-c_{1}},\ \ d_{0}=\frac{c_{1}-c_{2}}{2}-\frac{c_{0}^{2}}{14c_{1}^{2}}. (118)

Denote

F⁡(w)=(w−α)​(w−β)​(w2+d0),F(w)=(w-\alpha)(w-\beta)(w^{2}+d_{0}), (119)

and rewrite it as follows:

F⁡(w)=w4+p​w2+q​w+r,F(w)=w^{4}+pw^{2}+qw+r, (120)

p=d0−(α+β),r=−d0​(α+β),s=d0​α​β.\displaystyle p=d_{0}-(\alpha+\beta),\ \ r=-d_{0}(\alpha+\beta),\ \ s=d_{0}\alpha\beta. (121)

But because of special form of F⁡(w)F(w) (see Eq.(119)), we know that the case 1, case 2, case 6 and case 9 in section 3 are impossible to occur in the case of double Sine-Gordon equation. Other cases are possible. Thus we can give all traveling solutions to double Sine-Gordon equation according to the cases 3-5 and cases 7-8 in section 3. We omit them for briefly.

Example 5. Classification of all single traveling wave solutions to Pochharmer-Chree Equation ([35]) which reads

ut​t−α​ux​x+β​u+γ​u3+δ​u5.u_{tt}-\alpha u_{xx}+\beta u+\gamma u^{3}+\delta u^{5}. (122)

Takeing traveling wave transformation u=u⁡(ξ),ξ=k​x+ω​t,u=u(\xi),\xi=kx+\omega t, instituting it into Eq.(122) and integrating once yields

(u′)2=a3​u6+a2​u4+a1​u2+a0,(u^{\prime})^{2}=a_{3}u^{6}+a_{2}u^{4}+a_{1}u^{2}+a_{0}, (123)

a3=−δ3​(ω2−α​k2),a2=−γ2​(ω2−α​k2),a1=−βω2−α​k2,a_{3}=-\frac{\delta}{3(\omega^{2}-\alpha k^{2})},\ \ a_{2}=-\frac{\gamma}{2(\omega^{2}-\alpha k^{2})},\ \ a_{1}=-\frac{\beta}{\omega^{2}-\alpha k^{2}}, (124)

and a0a_{0} is an arbitrary constant. Let v=u2,v=u^{2}, then Eq.(123) becomes

(v′)2=2​v​(a3​v3+a2​v2+a1​v+a0).(v^{\prime})^{2}=2v(a_{3}v^{3}+a_{2}v^{2}+a_{1}v+a_{0}). (125)

Similar to the example 3, we can give all traveling wave solutions to Pochhamer-Chree equation (122). Because of special form of the right polynomial of Eq.(125), the case 1 and case 9 in section 3 are impossible to occur, all other cases 2-8 are possible. We omit them for simplicity.

Example 1: All traveling solutions to triple Sine-Gordon equation([3],[42-45])

ux​x−ut​t=c​sin⁡u+13​a​sin⁡13​u+23​b​sin⁡23​u,u_{xx}-u_{tt}=c\sin{u}+\frac{1}{3}a\sin{\frac{1}{3}u}+\frac{2}{3}b\sin{\frac{2}{3}u}, (179)

In Ref.[3], we used the similar idea to deal with it, but we didn’t recognize that its all single traveling wave solutions can be obtained. We give in the following its all traveling wave solutions.

Take traveling wave transformation

u=3​arccos⁡v.u=3\arccos{v}. (183)

Let

v=(8​c1)−15​w−b16​c1,ξ=13​(8​c1)15​ξ1.v=(8c_{1})^{-\frac{1}{5}}w-\frac{b_{1}}{6c_{1}},\ \ \xi=\frac{1}{3}(8c_{1})^{\frac{1}{5}}\xi_{1}. (185)

5 The solutions of irrational integrals and applications

There are some mathematical physics equations whose reduced ODE’s have the form of (u′)2=g⁡(u)f⁡(u)(u^{\prime})^{2}=\frac{g(u)}{f(u)}, where g⁡(u)g(u) and f⁡(u)f(u) are two polynomials. So the classifications of their all traveling wave solutions are more complex.

6 Classifications of solutions to some more general nonlinear differential equations

There are many nonlinear differential equations which can be reduced to an integrable ODE as follows

u′′​(ξ)+p⁡(u)​(u′​(ξ))2+q⁡(u)=0.u^{\prime\prime}(\xi)+p(u)(u^{\prime}(\xi))^{2}+q(u)=0. (219)

These equations include High order KdV equation([50])

ut+ux+α​u​ux+β​ux​x​x+α2​ρ1​u2​ux+α​β​(ρ2​u​ux​x​x+ρ3​ux​ux​x)=0;u_{t}+u_{x}+\alpha uu_{x}+\beta u_{xxx}+\alpha^{2}\rho_{1}u^{2}u_{x}+\alpha\beta(\rho_{2}uu_{xxx}+\rho_{3}u_{x}u_{xx})=0; (220)

Coupled KdV equation([51])

ut+ε1​vx+ε2​u2​ux+ε3​ux​x​x=0,\displaystyle u_{t}+\varepsilon_{1}v_{x}+\varepsilon_{2}u^{2}u_{x}+\varepsilon_{3}u_{xxx}=0, (221)
vt+η1​(u​v)x+η2​v​vx=0;\displaystyle v_{t}+\eta_{1}(uv)_{x}+\eta_{2}vv_{x}=0; (222)

Coupled mKdV equation([52])

ut+ε1​v​vx+ε2​u​ux+ε3​ux​x​x=0,\displaystyle u_{t}+\varepsilon_{1}vv_{x}+\varepsilon_{2}uu_{x}+\varepsilon_{3}u_{xxx}=0, (223)
vt+η1​(u​v)x+η2​v​vx=0,\displaystyle v_{t}+\eta_{1}(uv)_{x}+\eta_{2}vv_{x}=0, (224)

and so on. We give the general solution of the Eq.(219) in the following:

Lemma[53]: The general solution of ODE (219) is as follows:

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​uexp(−2∫p(u)du)[c−2∫q(u)exp(2∫p(u)du)du],\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\sqrt{\exp(-2\int p(u)\mathrm{d}u)[c-2\int q(u)\exp(2\int p(u)\mathrm{d}u)\mathrm{d}u]}}, (225)

where cc and ξ0\xi_{0} are two arbitrary constants.

We take the coupled KdV equation as an example to illustrate our method for shortly. Other equations can be dealt with similarly.

Case 2. c1≠0c_{1}\neq 0. According to the lemma, then vv satisfies the following integral form:

±(ξ−ξ0)=∫(v2−2​c1k​δ)​d​vv​a8​v8+⋯+a1​v+a0,\pm(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{(v^{2}-\frac{2c_{1}}{k\delta})\mathrm{d}v}{v\sqrt{a_{8}v^{8}+\cdots+a_{1}v+a_{0}}}, (237)

where a1,⋯,a8a_{1},\cdots,a_{8} can be expressed by the corresponding parameters. Denote F⁡(v)=a8​v8+⋯+a1​v+a0F(v)=a_{8}v^{8}+\cdots+a_{1}v+a_{0}, its complete discrimination system is too complex to write. We omit these solutions for briefly.

7 Discussions and conclusions

In Ref. [16], Fan proposed an expanse method to seek for the single traveling wave solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. His key idea is to assume that the solution has a polynomial form u=anϕn+⋅+a1ϕ+a0u=a_{n}\phi^{n}+\cdot+a_{1}\phi+a_{0} of a function ϕ\phi which satisfies an ODE as follows:

ϕ′=±crϕr+⋅+c1ϕ+c0,\phi^{\prime}=\pm\sqrt{c_{r}\phi^{r}+\cdot+c_{1}\phi+c_{0}}, (238)

According to the balance principle, a relation of nn and rr can be obtained. In his paper, Fan take a special case of r=4r=4 as an example to apply his method. In the end of his paper, he said ”we only have investigated a special case when r=4r=4. the proposed method can be extended to the cases when r>4r>4. The details for those cases will be investigated in our future works”. In fact, there are two problems need to answer. One problem is whether or no there exist new solutions in the cases of r>4r>4 for some equations. The second problem is how to prove some solutions are new in the cases of r>4r>4 if the equation considered can’t be directly reduced to an integral form.

According to the above analysis to direct integral method ,we can make a conclusion that there aren’t new solutions in the cases of r>4r>4 for those equations which can be directly reduced to an integral form. Thus we have answered the Fan’s first problem.

Direct integral method is very natural and simple for solving traveling wave solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. But it is just complete discrimination system for polynomial make direct integral method becomes an efficient and powerful method. A lot of nonlinear mathematical physics equations can be dealt with by direct integral method, their all traveling wave solutions can be classified. These complete results can’t be obtained by using of other methods. On the other hand, a lot of nonlinear evolution equations such as (1+1)-dimensional Boussinesq equation and (3+1)-dimensional KP equation and so on, can be reduced to integral forms by setting some integral constants to zeroes. For those equations, we can not give their all traveling wave solutions, but we can still obtain their abundant exact solutions. For example, we consider the (2+1)-dimensional boussinesq equation

ut​t−ux​x+3​(u2)x​x−ux​x​x​x−uy​y=0.u_{tt}-u_{xx}+3(u^{2})_{xx}-u_{xxxx}-u_{yy}=0. (239)

Instituting traveling wave transformation u=u⁡(ξ),ξ=k1​x+k2​y+ω​tu=u(\xi),\xi=k_{1}x+k_{2}y+\omega t into Eq.(239) and integrating twice yield

k14​u′′=(ω2−k12−k22)​u+3​k12​u2+c2​ξ+c1.k_{1}^{4}u^{\prime\prime}=(\omega^{2}-k_{1}^{2}-k_{2}^{2})u+3k_{1}^{2}u^{2}+c_{2}\xi+c_{1}. (240)

where c1c_{1} and c2c_{2} are two arbitrary constants. If we take c2=0c_{2}=0, then we can apply the direct integral method to it. In fact, integrating Eq.(240) once yields

±k12​(ξ−ξ0)=∫d​uk12​u3+(ω2−k12−k22)​u2+c1​u+c0,\pm k_{1}^{2}(\xi-\xi_{0})=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\sqrt{k_{1}^{2}u^{3}+(\omega^{2}-k_{1}^{2}-k_{2}^{2})u^{2}+c_{1}u+c_{0}}}, (241)

where c0c_{0} is an arbitrary constant. According to Ref.[19], we can easily to give classification of all solutions to Eq.(241). Thus it is easy to obtain abundant traveling wave solutions to Eq.(239). For briefly, we omit them.
